column1: # ---------------- WHY IT MATTERS, AND IT IS ONE FACT ABOUT COVERAGE ----------------
*** MOST AUSTRALIAN NEWSPAPERS IN TROVE STOP AT 1954. THE CANBERRA TIMES RUNS TO 1995. ***
column2: Australian newspaper digitisation halts at 1954 for copyright, which is why Trove is normally useless for a family that arrived in 1965. THE CANBERRA TIMES IS THE EXCEPTION, digitised 1926-1995, and the COMMONWEALTH OF AUSTRALIA GAZETTE runs 1901-1973. THE FAMILY LANDED IN CANBERRA. So this is the FIRST FREE INSTRUMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAS EVER HAD that reaches the Australian branch after the emigration.

column1: the control
column2: Canberra returns 5,029,116 articles. The instrument answers, and a zero from it is a zero from something that was working.

column1: # ---------------- *** THE FIND: THE MELBOURNE LEIBHOLZ IS NATURALISED IN 1944 *** ----------------
*** JOACHIM PETER LEIBHOLZ, 28 SEPTEMBER 1944 ***
column2: COMMONWEALTH OF AUSTRALIA GAZETTE No. 193, Thursday 28 September 1944, page 2212, "CERTIFICATES OF NATURALIZATION": "LEIBHOLZ, JOACHIM PETER, [6]7 WALSH-STREET, SOUTH YARRA, VICTORIA." The house number is OCR'd as "07" and is not read here; the street and suburb are plain.

column1: *** AND IT IS A SMALLER FIND THAN IT LOOKED, BECAUSE THIS ARCHIVE ALREADY HELD THE NATURALISATION ***
column2: The first draft of this row said "until now the Melbourne man was a name in a death index" and inferred his arrival from the five-year residence rule. BOTH WERE WRONG AND WERE CAUGHT BEFORE PUBLICATION BY READING THE PAGE THIS ARCHIVE HAS ALREADY WRITTEN. australia.astro has carried since 21 September: born Berlin 20 August 1903, LANDED AT MELBOURNE FROM THE ANCHISES ON 12 JUNE 1939, NATURALISED AT SOUTH YARRA ON 27 JULY 1944, previous nationality STATELESS — all from the NAA naturalisation card. The arrival is documented to the day, so inferring it from a residence rule adds nothing, and the naturalisation was never news.

column1: so what is actually new, stated at its real size
column2: TWO THINGS AND NOT MORE. (1) THE STREET: this archive had "South Yarra"; the gazette gives WALSH STREET, SOUTH YARRA. (2) THE GAZETTE CITATION ITSELF — Commonwealth of Australia Gazette No. 193 of 28 September 1944, page 2212 — WHICH IS A SECOND, PUBLIC, INDEPENDENT ATTESTATION of a fact previously resting on one NAA card. A card and a gazette, produced by different offices for different purposes, agreeing on man, suburb and year. THAT IS WORTH HAVING AND IT IS NOT A DISCOVERY.

column1: and the date moves by two months, which is the kind of thing that matters later
column2: THE CARD SAYS NATURALISED 27 JULY 1944; THE GAZETTE PUBLISHES IT ON 28 SEPTEMBER 1944. Those are not in conflict — a certificate is granted and then gazetted — but anyone reading only one of them will carry a date the other does not support, and this archive has spent the week on exactly that failure.

column1: what it does NOT do
column2: IT DOES NOT CONNECT THE MELBOURNE LANE TO SCHUBIN. Row 242 says that plainly about the death certificate and it is just as true here.

column1: # ---------------- *** AND THEN HIS OWN WORDS TURNED UP, WHICH BEAT THE GAZETTE *** ----------------
*** THE ARGUS, 18 FEBRUARY 1944 — A NOTICE OF INTENTION TO APPLY, PLACED BY THE MAN HIMSELF ***
column2: I, JOACHIM PETER LEIBHOLZ, of GERMAN nationality, born at BERLIN, Germany, and RESIDENT 4 YEARS 8 MONTHS IN AUSTRALIA, now residing at 67 WALSH STREET, SOUTH YARRA, VICTORIA, intend to Apply for Naturalisation under the Nationality Act 1920-1936. A paid newspaper advertisement, required by the Act, seven months before the gazette entry.

column1: it fixes the house number the gazette lost
column2: the gazette OCR reads "07 Walsh-street" and this archive declined to guess it. THE NOTICE PRINTS 67. Two documents, one unreadable and one clean, and the clean one settles it.

column1: *** AND IT CORROBORATES THE ANCHISES TO WITHIN DAYS, FROM A COMPLETELY INDEPENDENT DOCUMENT ***
column2: RESIDENT 4 YEARS 8 MONTHS IN FEBRUARY 1944 PUTS HIS ARRIVAL IN JUNE 1939. The NAA passenger record has him landing at Melbourne from the ANCHISES ON 12 JUNE 1939. A man counting his own months in a newspaper advertisement and a shipping list compiled by somebody else agree to within days. THIS IS WHAT THE EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS ROW TRIED TO GET FROM THE FIVE-YEAR RESIDENCE RULE AND COULD NOT: a real, independent, documentary corroboration instead of an inference.

column1: *** AND A DISCREPANCY WORTH KEEPING: HE SAID GERMAN, THE CLERK WROTE STATELESS ***
column2: The NAA naturalisation card gives his previous nationality as STATELESS, and australia.astro draws the right conclusion from it — the Reich made him stateless after he left. BUT IN HIS OWN NOTICE OF FEBRUARY 1944 HE DECLARES HIMSELF "OF GERMAN NATIONALITY". Both are true of the same man in the same year: the Eleventh Decree of November 1941 stripped the citizenship of Jews outside the Reich, and a man may write down the nationality he was born to while an official writes down the one the law left him. NOT A CONFLICT. A gap between what a person says he is and what a state says he is, on the same page of the same process.

column1: *** THE NAME HE ACTUALLY USED ***
column2: THE AGE, 2 October 1954, "People, Parties: Bohemian Setting for Ball": among guests entertained at a Toorak home before the ball, "MR. AND MRS. PETER LEIBHOLZ". He is Joachim Peter on every official document and PETER in Melbourne society. Searching Trove on JOACHIM finds the gazette; searching on PETER finds the man.

column1: the company is the point, not the party
column2: the same paragraph carries Nelken, Horowitz, Abry, Reschid Bey. A German-Jewish refugee of 1939 is at a Toorak ball in 1954 among other émigré names. FIFTEEN YEARS FROM STATELESS TO THE SOCIAL COLUMN.

column1: *** MRS. H. LEIBHOLZ, MELBOURNE, 1969 — AND THE ARCHIVE HAD A TILDE-OR-HILDE PROBLEM ***
column2: THE AUSTRALIAN JEWISH NEWS (Melbourne), 8 August 1969, p.24, WIZO Aliyah notes: "Welcome! Two ladies have just joined us — MRS. H. LEIBHOLZ and Mrs. E. Wolf are now our newest and most welcome members." australia.astro records his wife as "TILDE on one file, HILDE on another". AN INITIAL OF H SUPPORTS ONE READING AND NOT THE OTHER. It is not proof — H. is an initial, this is a different document type, and no document here ties this woman to that household beyond surname, city and community — BUT IT IS THE ONLY THIRD VOICE THE QUESTION HAS.

column1: a daughter, and she is not pursued
column2: THE AUSTRALIAN WOMEN'S WEEKLY, 31 July 1968: "Dr. JANE LEIBHOLZ weds STEWART WALLACE, Press Attache with the Prime Minister's Department in Canberra. The bride, who is the DAUGHTER OF MR. AND MRS. PETER LEIBHOLZ, is a lecturer in Animal Husbandry at the University of Sydney." St John's, Toorak, reception at Nine Darling Street, South Yarra. SHE MAY WELL BE LIVING AND SHE IS NOT IN THIS ARCHIVE'S TREE — the Melbourne lane is not kin and has never been claimed as kin. Recorded because it is a public announcement in a national magazine and because it shows the household had children; NOT FOLLOWED FURTHER, and nobody is approached.

column1: # ---------------- *** THE SPONSOR AT HACKETT NOW HAS A STREET *** ----------------
*** MARQUARDT, ANNE MARIE, 2 KENNY PLACE, HACKETT, NATURALISED 28.9.66 ***
column2: Commonwealth of Australia Gazette, 9 March 1967, "Certificates of Naturalisation". THE 1965 NOMINAL ROLL FORWARDS THE LUWINSKI FAMILY C/O MR H. MARQUARDT AT HACKETT, ACT, and row 215 says flatly that WHAT DECIDES THE SPONSOR QUESTION IS AN ADDRESS. There is now a Marquardt household at Hackett with a street and a number.

column1: and H. MARQUARDT HIMSELF IS NOT IN THESE LISTS, which is checked and not assumed
column2: five further Commonwealth Gazette naturalisation lists were read for MARQUARDT — 15 Feb 1968, 29 Feb 1968, 24 Apr 1968, 18 Jan 1971, 27 Dec 1973. EVERY ONE IS SOMEWHERE ELSE: Marie and Heinrich Marquardt at 376 Pittwater Road, NORTH RYDE, NSW; Ray Marquardt at West Hoxton, NSW; Jill Marquardt at Longreach, QUEENSLAND; Andreas Marquardt at Montrose, VICTORIA. NONE AT HACKETT AND NONE IN THE ACT. If H. Marquardt arrived on the ANNA SALEN in March 1955, as row 215's best candidate did, he would have been eligible to naturalise around 1960 — BEFORE the lists that survive here. The absence is explained and is not evidence against him.

column1: # ---------------- ONE LEAD THAT PAID NOTHING ----------------
the FLAVIA, ex Bremerhaven, arriving 17 September 1965
column2: searched and NOT FOUND. Trove's shipping coverage collapses after 1954 with the newspapers, and the Canberra Times does not print Sydney arrival lists. The twelve "Flavia Bremerhaven" hits are all DUTCH AUSTRALIAN WEEKLY advertisements of 1964 for the same ship on other voyages. THE ARRIVAL REMAINS DOCUMENTED ONLY BY THE NOMINAL ROLL, and Trove adds nothing to it.

column1: # ---------------- TWO WARNINGS ABOUT THE INSTRUMENT, BOTH LEARNED THE SAME HOUR ----------------
*** TROVE NORMALISES SPELLING, SO A TROVE SEARCH IS NOT A SPELLING TEST ***
column2: Luwinski and "Luwinsky" RETURN THE IDENTICAL NINE ARTICLES. The search engine stems and fuzzes; it is not matching the string you typed. THIS ARCHIVE HAS SPENT A FORTNIGHT ON THE PRINCIPLE THAT DIFFERENT SPELLINGS ARE DIFFERENT SLOTS, and Trove quietly refuses to honour it. To know which spelling is actually on the page you must open the page.

column1: and a reading fault that was mine, not the instrument's
column2: the first sweep printed EIGHT rows and the total said NINE, and the ninth — the Commonwealth Gazette citizenship list, the most valuable of the nine — was the one below the fold. THE TOTAL WAS CORRECT AND VISIBLE BOTH TIMES. tools/trove.py now prints the TOTAL on every search, above the rows, because a row count you chose is not a result count.

column1: # ---------------- *** AND WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT PUBLISHED *** ----------------
*** THE CANBERRA SEAM IS REAL, IT IS EIGHT ARTICLES, AND IT IS ALMOST ENTIRELY ABOUT LIVING PEOPLE ***
column2: Of the nine "Luwinski" hits, EIGHT ARE THE CANBERRA TIMES BETWEEN 1970 AND 1987 — technical college results, weekend sporting round-ups, family notices, advertising, a 1987 court list. That is exactly where the 1965 emigration roll and the Marquardt sponsorship at Hackett said the family would be, so the instrument has found them. IT HAS ALSO FOUND THEIR CHILDREN, who are living, and who this archive does not name or approach.

column1: so the finding is recorded and the detail is not
column2: The addresses, the citizenship date, the engagement notice and the married surname are in notes/, which is gitignored, and they stay there. WHAT CAN BE SAID IN PUBLIC IS THIS: the family were settled in CANBERRA by 1972; a Commonwealth of Australia Gazette citizenship series documents them there; and a Canberra Times family notice of January 1973 attests that MANFRED AND HELGA WERE BOTH ALIVE AND IN CANBERRA at that date. Nothing further.

column1: MANFRED HIMSELF IS NOT IN TROVE
column2: a search on his full name returns ZERO. He died at Brisbane in 2012, long past the Canberra Times's 1995 cut-off, and Queensland papers of that date are not digitised at all. ROW 213'S RYERSON INDEX REMAINS THE ONLY FREE INSTRUMENT THAT REACHES HIS DEATH, and it is still returning "Server Overloaded".
